text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Due to the rising number of people on early retirement the financial ministry now estimates that 155,000 Danes will retire early by the year 2005, twice as many as expected one year ago.

--- A new survey made by Gallup for Berlingske Tidende shows that 95 percent of Danish consumers think that genetically engineered food should be clearly marked and 68 percent believe that it should be banned altogether.
--- Swedish telecom company Netcom now wants to break telecom group Tele Danmark's cable monopoly by investing in its own infrastructure of fibre-optic cables in Denmark.

--- For the first time ever Danish shipping companies place more orders abroad than with troubled Danish shipyards, with orders in October for 45 ships worth 7.6 billion crowns built abroad and only 15 ships worth 6.8 billion crowns built in Denmark.

--- In spite of an increase in domestic passengers of 9 percent in the first nine months of 1996, SAS is losing thousands of passengers on Danish internal flights to its ally Cimber Air and to rivals British Airways and Maersk Air.

--- From January 1, 1997 retired Danes living in Britain are no longer to get state pensions from Denmark without paying taxes to the Danish state as a consequence of a new double taxation agreement between Denmark and Britain.
